font/msdf_font.description: Load a local font and a named font as distance-field atlases.
walkthrough: FontLoader.msdf prepares font resources asynchronously before SDFText is constructed. The local TTF path and named Fira Code request exercise different ways to locate the font.
Each text entity receives its loaded atlas and its own fill. Font loading can fail independently of scene geometry, so inspect the requested font resource when one label is missing.
experiments: Replace the local TTF with another available font, keeping the text and font size unchanged. Compare glyph shapes and spacing.

fourier/fourier_demo.description: Reconstruct a path with rotating Fourier vectors and a fading trace.
walkthrough: FourierEpicycles and FourierPresets are local example helpers, not exports from the core Retiam package. The preset supplies a sampled outline; Fourier coefficients produce rotating vectors whose sum traces that outline. Circles visualize vector magnitudes, arrows show directions, and the tip supplies the point followed by TracePath.

The scene begins with the IndiaMap preset and a small harmonic count. Its updater does not add a constant number per second: it calculates Math.pow(time, 1.5) / 40000 and caps the result at 600. Adding higher-frequency terms makes small features easier to recover, while increasing the amount of vector geometry and computation.

The same updater increases speed and shortens trace age until its lower condition is reached. Those are independent changes: harmonics affect the approximation, speed affects traversal, and age affects how much history remains visible. Freeze two of them before judging the third.

Camera follow runs in the post phase, after the Fourier entity has updated. localToWorld converts the local tip into the camera’s world-space target. Following an unconverted tip would break if the epicycle container were translated or scaled. The separate 100 ms updater only refreshes DOM statistics.

The panel changes presets, harmonic count, tip appearance, trace age and circle visibility. The automatic updater can overwrite a manually selected harmonic count on the next update; focusing the slider only suppresses its displayed value refresh. Disable the automatic harmonic assignment to make a stable comparison.

The local pause button sets Fourier speed to zero, whereas scene pause affects the engine clock. The reset button clears the trace and restores progress; it does not reconstruct the whole application. When reusing the helper, keep coefficient preparation separate from per-frame geometry updates and give DOM controls their own cleanup lifetime.
experiments: Comment out the automatic setHarmonics call, then compare 10, 50 and 200 harmonics at a fixed speed and trace age.
Disable the post-phase follow callback and translate the Fourier container. Observe the difference between a fixed view and a camera following a world-space tip.

geometry_raytracing_3d/builder_3d_demo.description: Drag textured planes and spatial meshes over a shadow-receiving ground.
walkthrough: Canvas-generated text and hollow shapes become textures on flat planes. A sphere and a Builder3D star provide actual spatial geometry beside those textured silhouettes.
Hover handlers change scale and emission; dragging changes position. The updater avoids rotating the actively dragged object, preventing scripted movement from competing with pointer input.
experiments: Drag a textured plane beside the sphere and orbit the camera. Compare their thickness and silhouettes from the side.

geometry_raytracing_3d/builder_demo2.description: Arrange thin boxes in front of a wall and watch their shadows change.
walkthrough: The objects are narrow Box meshes, with a wall and floor as receiving surfaces. A floating frame introduces an additional shadow across the arrangement.
The updater changes transforms, while lighting and materials determine the resulting appearance. Apparent depth comes from geometry, viewpoint and shadows together.
experiments: Increase one box’s depth from 0.2 to 2. Compare its side silhouette and shadow without changing its front dimensions.

geometry_raytracing_3d/depth_map.description: Generate a terrain mesh from heightmap samples.
walkthrough: Terrain3D defines the terrain extent and sampling resolution. generateFromHeightmap awaits the image-driven generation before adding the terrain to the scene.
The material and texture mapping style the resulting mesh. The source has a fallback for image failure, so a visible terrain alone does not prove that the intended heightmap loaded.
experiments: Change widthSegments while keeping the same heightmap. Inspect how coarse sampling affects ridges and the mesh silhouette.

geometry_raytracing_3d/mouse_trace.description: Turn pointer positions into a spatial orb and a fading trail.
walkthrough: Scene mouse events update a shared target position. The orb follows that position, and TracePath samples it through targetFunc instead of receiving a new path string on every event.
The trace retains recent motion and can be cleared on pointer down. Camera orientation affects the input mapping, so inspect the result from a stable view first.
experiments: Draw a slow loop and then a fast one. Change trace age to compare retained history without changing pointer handling.

geometry_raytracing_3d/plugin_system_dem.description: Compose a motion plugin and an outline plugin around differently shaded models.
walkthrough: The custom BobAndRotatePlugin installs motion through the scene’s plugin lifecycle. OutlinePlugin adds a rendering treatment without requiring each mesh to implement outlining.
Press O after focusing the preview to toggle inking. Material shading remains on the objects, while plugin installation and removal control scene-level behavior.
experiments: Remove BobAndRotatePlugin while keeping OutlinePlugin active. Compare static outlined geometry with the original moving scene.

geometry_raytracing_3d/shadow_map_transp.description: Compare cutout textures with an opaque mesh in shadow mapping.
walkthrough: Canvas-generated grate and leaf textures contain transparent regions. Their models cast and receive shadows alongside a solid sphere and ground plane.
Dragging changes light-space placement; hover emission changes the visible object rather than the texture’s alpha mask. Inspect both the surface silhouette and the corresponding ground shadow.
experiments: Fill the grate texture’s transparent holes and replay. Compare the object and shadow silhouettes with the cutout version.

geometry_raytracing_3d/shadow_map.description: Reuse a generated canvas texture on a box and a sprite.
walkthrough: The source draws a texture with Canvas2D, then supplies it to a spatial Box and a flat Sprite. The same image therefore participates in different geometry paths.
Pointer handlers enable dragging and hover styling while an updater rotates the box. Ground shadows expose the difference between an image-bearing surface and a spatial volume.
experiments: Replace the texture’s central motif with a circle. Compare its appearance on the rotating box with the flat sprite.

geometry_raytracing_3d/styles_and_shadow.description: Compare PBR, Gooch, cel and clay-style materials under shared lighting.
walkthrough: Separate objects demonstrate each treatment: PBR responds through physical material parameters, Gooch uses warm–cool illustration, and cel shading introduces discrete lighting bands.
The ground receives shadows while the objects rotate. Shared lighting makes the styles comparable, but their differing geometry still affects highlights and shadow shape.
experiments: Apply the Gooch setup to the box as well as the sphere. Compare materials on a shared geometry before comparing different shapes.

graphs/automata_dfa_demo.description: Follow a DFA as it reads two strings and reports acceptance.
walkthrough: Automaton defines states and transitions; Tape presents the input and current read position. AutomatonRunner connects those structures during execution.
The two awaited runs make different outcomes visible. Animation duration controls presentation speed; transition definitions determine acceptance.
experiments: Change one input string by a single bit. Follow the exact transition where its state path diverges.

graphs/graph_theory_demo.description: Animate a weighted network through several layouts and a highlighted route.
walkthrough: Nodes and weighted edges define topology. Force-directed, circular and layered layouts change positions while retaining those connections.

The highlighted A-to-G route is specified in the scene. The labels describe shortest-path behavior, but this example’s active presentation should not be mistaken for a live Dijkstra search on every frame.
experiments: Change an edge weight, then inspect the explicitly selected path. Update the route or add a path-finding calculation before claiming a new shortest path.

highlights/circumscribe_demo.description: Draw temporary and retained boundary highlights around existing entities.
walkthrough: Circumscribe derives a surrounding contour from the target’s bounds. The box, circle and title show how contour shape and padding affect emphasis.
The highlight is an additional visual layer; it does not replace the target’s paint or geometry. Persistent settings determine whether that layer remains after the animation.
experiments: Increase padding around the box while keeping stroke width fixed. Compare breathing room with line thickness.

highlights/color_tint_demo.description: Tint a grouped card temporarily, then leave a new accent color.
walkthrough: ColorTint changes the target’s fill and stroke through the animation. Applying it to the group includes the card and its label rather than only the background rectangle.
The first tint restores the original treatment; the second demonstrates a retained accent. Restoration matters when later animations expect the original colors.
experiments: Tint only the card rectangle instead of the whole group. Compare label contrast during the same color transition.

highlights/corner_brackets_demo.description: Frame a whole card and then a smaller header with animated brackets.
walkthrough: CornerBrackets places L-shaped marks around target bounds. Targeting the card group includes its contents, while targeting the header produces a tighter frame.
Padding, bracket length and stroke width describe the framing marks independently of the target’s appearance. The marks do not alter the card’s dimensions.
experiments: Use the header as the first target and increase padding. Compare target selection with padding around the larger group.

highlights/flash_demo.description: Emit radial rays around an entity and a coordinate point.
walkthrough: Flash can resolve its center from the target group or receive an explicit position. The two calls show attention directed at an object and at an otherwise empty location.
Ray count, length and timing control the burst. The target remains intact after the effect; the flash is a transient accent rather than a geometric transformation.
experiments: Move the explicit flash coordinate to the orb’s edge and reduce ray count. Compare a localized cue with a centered burst.

highlights/marker_sweep_demo.description: Sweep a translucent marker behind text and retain selected emphasis.
walkthrough: MarkerSweep uses target bounds to define the highlighter region. The example text is scene typography; the displayed import string is not executed as code.
The first highlight is transient and the second remains. Color and opacity must leave enough contrast for the underlying glyphs to stay readable.
experiments: Lower the persistent marker’s opacity and replace the phrase with a shorter one. Inspect both contrast and bound-based sizing.

highlights/shimmer_sweep_demo.description: Pass a bright sheen across newly introduced text.
walkthrough: The text first grows into view, then ShimmerSweep supplies a separate finishing accent. Separating the two animations gives the reader time to recognize the content.
The sheen changes the visible highlight over the glyphs without changing their positions or the formula string. Its timing should support reading rather than compete with it.
experiments: Double the delay before the shimmer, keeping its duration fixed. Compare how easily the formula can be read before the accent.

highlights/underline_demo.description: Compare straight and wavy emphasis beneath text.
walkthrough: Underline derives its placement from the selected text. The straight line reads as ordinary emphasis; the wavy variant can suggest a warning or a marked expression.
Both examples retain their underlines after drawing. Stroke width and vertical spacing affect readability independently of the text’s font size.
experiments: Apply both variants to the same phrase with the same stroke width. Compare their meaning and visual weight.

hybrid_pipelines/hybrid_mix.description: Mix a raytraced glass sphere, a rasterized cube and a vector path.
walkthrough: The models select their rendering path through RT_ENABLE. The glass sphere exercises raytracing while the opaque cube uses rasterization.
The vector Path adds a different kind of geometry to the same composition. Combining paths requires compatible lighting, depth and transparency behavior rather than merely matching object positions.
experiments: Disable RT_ENABLE on the sphere and compare its glass appearance. Keep camera and lighting unchanged during the comparison.

instancing/instanced_active_range.description: Reuse a fixed instance pool as particles are spawned and retired.
walkthrough: Instanced allocates capacity once; CPU particle state supplies position, velocity, rotation and color. activeCount and firstInstance select the live portion of that pool.
The ring-buffer arrangement reuses records instead of allocating a new entity for each particle. Integration timestep and gravity control motion separately from pool bookkeeping.
experiments: Reduce pool capacity and raise spawn rate. Watch records being reused before changing particle motion.

instancing/instanced_interactive_picking.description: Hover and select individual instances in a shared mesh group.
walkthrough: One Instanced entity holds the grid. RaycastHit identifies the touched instance, allowing event handlers to update its color and selected-state membership.

Selection survives hover changes because the scene tracks selected indices separately. updateInstances uploads the edited records; a shared template alone cannot hold distinct per-instance selections.
experiments: Click two instances, then hover a third. Change the selected color and verify that hover does not erase the existing selections.

instancing/instanced_non_uniform_scale.description: Stretch and orient instances toward an attractor.
walkthrough: The extended instance layout provides separate x, y and z scale values. setInstanceScale3D turns a shared cube into a needle or slab without duplicating its mesh.
The updater computes orientation and deformation from the attractor position. Pointer input can move that attractor, separating a shared force field from individual geometry storage.
experiments: Keep the attractor fixed and make all three scale components equal. Compare uniform scaling with the original anisotropic field.

instancing/instanced_partial_streaming.description: Update local regions of a large grid after pointer interaction.
walkthrough: The grid begins with one full upload. Pointer hits create pulses; subsequent updates change affected instance ranges rather than intentionally rewriting every record.
Dirty ranges reduce upload work when most records stay still. The configured 40,000 instances demonstrate scale, but performance depends on the GPU and pulse workload.
experiments: Reduce the grid to 2,500 instances, then enlarge a pulse radius. Compare the affected region before testing the larger grid.

instancing/instanced_staggered_animation.description: Reveal a spiral of instances with per-instance timing offsets.
walkthrough: The source computes a Fibonacci distribution and stores final transforms. animateStaggered drives the entrance from those records without creating thousands of separate scene animations.
Its overshoot easing gives a spring-like appearance; it is an easing formula rather than a simulated spring system. A later updater adds a continuing wave.
experiments: Increase stagger spacing while keeping the individual duration fixed. Compare cascade length with the overshoot amount.
